members.title: FAA issues nationwide ground-stop order, delaying or canceling nearly 7,000 flights
members.lead: Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, said the airspace was now open and the problem had been identified Chaos at US airports as stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted a nationwide ground stop that was declared Friday afternoon, delaying or canceling more than 11,000 US flights, according to aviation tracker FlightAware, and throwing airports into sudden chaos. The FAA confirmed the airspace was open in an advisory on its website. “So at 8.15 tonight, Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. “But it’s going to take us some time to unwind what’s happened this afternoon.” Continue reading...

members.title: What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA
members.lead: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop for all planes due to take off in the US, delaying and canceling thousands of flights Flights grounded at all US airports due to communications outage – live The US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration said in a statement that the nationwide halt to departures and delays to landings at all US airports that began at about 4pm ET on Friday was caused by “a temporary telecommunications outage”. “Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA added. members.title: US-bound flights out of Australia delayed after telecommunications outage grounded American planes
members.lead: Sydney and Melbourne airports say flights were affected by now-lifted ban on departures in US US flight outage – live updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Some US bound flights from Sydney Airport were grounded or delayed on Saturday after to American authorities halted departures and delayed landings at all US airports. Flights from Melbourne Airport were also affected, with travel for passengers expected to depart for Los Angeles shortly after 10am being delayed by more than two hours. Continue reading...
